With all four modules tied at exactly 1573 the 0.5 point tie-break window never opens, so the strict per-question argmax is degenerate: simulated directly it placed 42 of 50 questions in Paediatrics L3 and Obstetrics L3, allocated nothing to Psychiatry or Medicine, and would have taken the module spread from 0 to 25, breaching the Section 2 requirement that all four modules stay within about 10 of each other. This is the sixth consecutive fire to record that degeneracy. This fire therefore allocated across all four modules and steered the tier mix by the within-module deficit, which is what the tie-break clause points at when it defers to the Section 2 module-balance rule. L5 was not generated because its deficit is negative in every module; adding L5 would move that tier further above target rather than towards it.
